concepts.def: Letting go of resentment for a wrong done to you
The death penalty — execution as state punishment
Bringing offender and victim together to repair harm
Unpaid work in the community as punishment
Fixed punishments set by the Qur'an for serious crimes

walkthroughs.body_html:
Jesus taught radical forgiveness — 'seventy-seven times' (Matthew 18:22).

The Lord's Prayer: 'Forgive us our trespasses as we forgive those who trespass against us' (Matthew 6:12).

The Qur'an says 'Repel evil with what is better' (41:34) and praises those who pardon others.

The UK abolished the death penalty for murder in 1965 (completely 1998). The Roman Catholic Church now teaches the death penalty is 'inadmissible' (Catechism, updated 2018).

Some Christians point to Genesis 9:6 to support it. In Islamic teaching, qisas (retaliation) is permitted for murder but the family can forgive (Qur'an 2:178).

Restorative justice brings offender and victim together to repair harm. Many Christians see this as embodying gospel values of forgiveness and reconciliation.

Community service, prison and fines are common UK responses. Reformation programmes (education, therapy) reflect a Christian and Islamic concern for redemption.
